Subject: Slate selection + context windowing — next steps for onboarding

Hi Ari —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Moving this into the inbox so we can lock the model slate and token plan ahead of our technical kickoff. Quick recap and asks so the CS/implementation team can finalize the mutual action plan: 

- Proposed shortlist (engineering-friendly names):
  • small-gen (Redwood-optimized 7B FP16 / q4_0) — lower latency, better for short completions
  • med-chat (Redwood-optimized 13B with 8k context) — balance for chat and structured extraction
  • long-context (32k-window variant, quantized) — for your multi-document summarization flows

- Context window needs: you mentioned aggregating up to ~18k tokens (multi-doc) for the Summarize flow and ~2–3k tokens for single-turn chat. Can you confirm typical doc sizes and whether you expect the 18k case to be the norm or a rare peak?

- Traffic & token volume estimate request: please attach a short sample of session-level events (per-interaction token counts and counts of calls/day). I attached a stub (cressida_session_samples.csv) in case helpful — you can replace with production numbers.

What we'll do on our side this week: Monica will map those traffic profiles to an initial capacity plan with per-model throughput targets and an estimated token cost delta across the three slate options. Grace will draft the rollout plan (canary thresholds + fallback model mapping) and Ben will add quantization/latency tradeoffs.

Next steps: if you can confirm the two items below by EOD Thursday, we can schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff next week and lock the MAP.

1) Confirm the 18k multi-doc frequency (rare / occasional / frequent) and average doc length.
2) Share a 7-day sample of session token counts (CSV or paste).

Attachments: cressida_session_samples.csv (placeholder)

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear summary. Happy to confirm and share samples. Quick answers/notes: 

- About the 18k window: that's an upper-case scenario for our Research Notes product. Frequency: we expect ~5% of user sessions to hit >12k tokens, ~1% to exceed ~18k. Typical summarize jobs are 3–8k tokens.

- Average doc length: source docs are usually 1.2–4.5k tokens (PDF pages + extracted text). Multi-doc summaries combine 2–6 docs.

- Traffic: baseline is 120k calls/month today (mostly low-tok chat). Forecasted ramp during Q3 launch: 350–450k calls/month with 10–12% of calls being summarize flows. Peak concurrency: ~80 QPS during daytime; sustained 25–30 QPS otherwise.

I'll drop a sanitized 7-day sample to procurement and to you by EOD. One question for the team: for the long-context 32k variant, what is your fallback mapping if the model is busy? Can you auto-route to med-chat with a truncation strategy, or do you offer incremental summarization to keep latency within SLA?

Also including procurement at procurement@cressida.ai so they see the MAP & SLA notes early.

—Ari
Ari Stern
Head of Product
Cressida AI
ari@cressida.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Slate selection + context windowing — next steps for onboarding

Thanks Ari — very helpful. Based on your numbers I sketched an initial capacity & token allocation plan (attached as MAP_v1). High-level notes below and a couple of asks.

- Recommended onboarding slate and routing policy:
  1) med-chat (13B, 8k) — default for chat & single-doc summarize; covers ~80% of calls.
  2) small-gen — fallback for low-latency short completions (templates, quick replies).
  3) long-context (32k) — reserved for rare multi-doc summarization; we propose a burst pool + queued incremental summarization fallback.

- Routing/fallback approach: if long-context capacity unavailable, route to med-chat with a preflight incremental-summary step: i) create 2–4 chunked summaries of the multi-doc input ii) concatenate and summarize to final. This reduces cost and preserves SLA for 95% of >12k jobs.

- Cost delta estimate (very rough): using your forecasted Q3 volumes, moving 10% of summarize traffic from med-chat to long-context increases token cost by ~38% but reduces average latency on multi-doc jobs by ~45%. We'll include a detailed per-token cost table in MAP_v1.

Asks: 
1) Please confirm whether you will accept incremental summarization (chunk+merge) as a behavioral fallback for >18k cases.
2) Share sample auth/header format for signed requests (we need to validate KV cache behavior with your auth flow).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx, sla-exceptions-questions.pdf

I'll populate the Drive MAP and HubSpot deal this afternoon (links below). If the above looks good, let's put a 60-minute technical kickoff on the calendar for next Tue/Wed.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
